mechanicalMeaning: Synexia source names are donor/reference names; M3JDK uses its own M3 names and preserves semantics/structure rather than copying identifiers blindly.
Synexia com.synexia.indexstring.MIndexString maps to the M3JDK internal java.lang.M3String counterpart.
The M3JDK java.lang.String representation is defined in terms of its internal M3String value owner rather than an optional MIndex sidecar.
M3String preserves the donor owner+coordinate model; per-value byte arrays, char arrays, segment arrays and offset/end arrays are not canonical M3String payload.
All M3JDK precompute facts, tables, caches, images and prepared plans are internal implementation details and are not part of java.lang.String or other public JDK API contracts.
Precompute reuse is bound to exact M3 owner/identity plus range/composition coordinates and cannot alias across owners merely by numeric ID or equal text.
Derived precompute never becomes a second text payload and absence of precompute cannot alter exact Java String semantics.
JNI/native byte[], char[], UTF-8 and UTF-16 representations are shadows materialized from M3String and are never retained as canonical String/M3String storage.
M3JDK internal precompute owners may use compact M3 names; donor class names are provenance/mapping evidence, not target ABI requirements.
Canonical M3String tuple composition is maintained as a bounded-height persistent DAG; repeated concat/repeat may not form an unbounded rope chain.
Binary-tree grouping is not canonical identity; the same ordered terminal M3 atom owner/range coordinate sequence converges to one canonical tuple owner.

Canonical tuple identity is structural over M3 owner/range coordinates, not java.lang.String content equality; equal UTF-16 spelling built from a different canonical coordinate structure may remain distinct.
Shape-independent Java-hash/length/coder plus logical edge-sample routing narrows candidates only; exact terminal owner/range verification decides canonical reuse, so collisions change cost only.

Reusable Maven/OpenRewrite atomization, patternization/IOP, documentation, scope, convergence, donor-review and mastery semantics are canonical in hsoliwal/com.synexia; M3JDK consumes exact pinned handoffs.

A reusable recipe body present in M3JDK is a compatibility mirror, thin activation, fixture or proof bound to an exact Synexia revision/blob and cannot become an independently edited semantic authority.
A reusable recipe defect or enhancement discovered while working in M3JDK is corrected and mastered in Synexia first, then re-exported through a new content-addressed handoff before target promotion.
Exact OpenJDK backport/preimage recipes, JDK API/ABI/native/runtime/jtreg integration and target-specific admission remain M3JDK-owned because their semantics depend on the JDK product tree.
A3 FILE-local reusable atomize-patternize-document convergence executes the pinned Synexia canonical recipe; the frozen legacy com.m3.rewrite family is not the A3 semantic authority.

Borrowing Apache-2.0 Synexia recipes transfers reusable mechanics only; M3JDK retains product naming, compatibility, configure/make, jtreg/runtime/JNI/HotSpot/GC/JIT/CDS proof and final serial promotion.
